newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares soften in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares soften in thin volume.

text.p: Istanbul stocks traded in narrow ranges and ended a shade lower as a downward correction, which has followed the recent steep rally, continued on Thursday, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed down three points, or 0.15 percent, at 2,006 after moving between 1,989 and 2,019.

It has now lost 1.8 percent in three days of profit-taking after soaring 30.5 percent between June 18, when the former Islamist-led coalition government resigned, and last Monday when it closed at an all-time high of 2,043.
The downward correction started on Tuesday after the new coalition won a confidence vote in parliament on Saturday.
Daily turnover fell to a two-week low of 20.78 trillion lira ($134.6 million), compared to Wednesday's 24.06 trillion lira.

Brokers said blue chip shares in state and energy firms which have a strong impact on the calculation of the market index because of their big market capitalisations were almost untouched, leaving the index stayed flat today.
They said the short-term technical correction was not expected to produce major losses.

"High overnight (money and repo) rates in the last two days also had a negative impact on the bourse. I expect the index to start an upward move prompted by mid-year profit prospects of firms due to be released soon," said Sinan Kesikbas from Iktisat Securities.
"Technically, there's no danger as long as the index stays above the 2,000 mark," he concluded.
Several brokers said they expected sideways trade to persist amid selective activity because the current level of turnover was too weak to carry the index to new records.

Of the 248 shares traded, gainers outdid losers by 125 to 63 and 60 closed steady. The IMKB Industrial inched up 0.42 percent to 1,933, the IMKB Services firmed 0.52 percent to 1,926 and the IMKB Financial eased down 0.19 percent to 2,155.
The index representing the food and beverages sector was the leading gainer with a 3.61 percent rise while the insurance sector was the top loser with a 3.24 percent loss.
The most active stocks of the day were Is Bank's C series, unchanged at 63,000 lira and Makina Takim, up 100 lira at 1,700. They made up 8.4 percent of the total volume.
